## Overview

Gemma 4's vision tower becomes a native vLLM tower that packs images and video frames with `cu_seqlens` instead of padding them, so it runs on any `--mm-encoder-attn-backend` (#43178, review of #43440).

Not a duplicate: #60577 keeps SDPA with a mask and is superseded; #60478 patches the transformers tower this PR removes. Tower LoRA (#42662) keeps working: same weight names.

## Claims

- Native tower from vLLM layers (`MMEncoderAttention`, `get_rope` + `ApplyRotaryEmb`, moonvit's packed merger); same checkpoints, no mapper. Reused by DiffusionGemma and EmbeddingGemma2.
- MMStar unchanged (within 1 point); TTFT up to 7% lower with the default backend and 6-17% lower with `TRITON_ATTN`, which picks up gfx1151's encoder attention work (#56450).
- Encoder CUDA graphs follow token budgets like Qwen3-VL.
- Packed `TORCH_SDPA` under `cudagraph_mm_encoder` now fails at startup with a clear error (it used to fail with a device-copy error during capture).

## Validation

gfx1151, PR on c1d8fade8d vs that commit ("main"); since rebased cleanly on 81a2879403.

| Model | MMStar: same answer as main | MMStar main / PR | TTFT main / PR, SDPA (ms) | TTFT main / PR, `TRITON_ATTN` (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemma-4-E2B-it | 283 / 300 | 37.3 / 37.7 % | 148.7 / 148.0 | 148.6 / 133.5 |
| gemma-4-E4B-it | 295 / 300 | 55.3 / 54.3 % | 203.5 / 202.2 | 203.3 / 187.0 |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it AWQ | 284 / 300 | 59.0 / 58.3 % | 465.8 / 433.0 | 465.8 / 388.7 |
| gemma-4-31B-it AWQ | 299 / 300 | 63.0 / 63.0 % | 1186.9 / 1158.0 | 1189.2 / 1114.7 |

MMStar: first 300 questions, greedy, 64 tokens. TTFT: one 336x336 image per request, median of 15, stdev ≤ 6.6 ms (1024x800 gives the same gains). Scripts below.

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4_unified.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/test_gemma4_vision.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_embedding_gemma2.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_mha_attn.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py          # 172 passed (*)
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_common.py -k gemma4   # 2 passed
pytest tests/lora/test_gemma4_tp.py::test_gemma4_lora                # passed
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py \
  -k "gemma4 or qwen2_5_vl or qwen3_vl"   # 6 passed with TRITON_ATTN (**)
```

(*) `test_mha_attn_platform[hip]` deselected: needs `flash_attn`, fails the same on main.
(**) gfx1151 defaults to `TORCH_SDPA`, which now stops with the new error; on main Qwen2.5-VL fails there with "Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA graph capture".

Also checked: encoder graph replay matches eager (images, videos, oversized items); `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` passes; `--dtype float16` on 26B AWQ works.
Not run: FLASH_ATTN, FLASHINFER (no CUDA hardware; CI covers the default backends) and online FP8 (no kernel on gfx1151).

```python
# mmstar.py MODEL OUT.json: first 300 MMStar questions, greedy, 64 tokens.
# Needs mmstar.parquet from https://huggingface.co/datasets/Lin-Chen/MMStar
import io, json, os, re, sys
os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0"
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
from PIL import Image
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

def letter(text):
    text = text.strip()
    m = (re.match(r"\(?([A-D])(?:$|[\s.:)])", text)
         or re.search(r"(?:answer|option)(?: is)?[:\s*]*\(?([A-D])\b", text, re.I)
         or re.search(r"\*\*\(?([A-D])[:.)*]", text))
    return m.group(1) if m else None

model, out = sys.argv[1:3]
rows = pq.read_table("mmstar.parquet").to_pylist()[:300]
llm = LLM(model=model, max_model_len=4096, max_num_seqs=8,
          limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1}, gpu_memory_utilization=0.85, seed=0)
msgs = [[{"role": "user", "content": [
    {"type": "image_pil", "image_pil": Image.open(io.BytesIO(r["image"])).convert("RGB")},
    {"type": "text", "text": r["question"] + "\nAnswer with the option's letter."}]}]
    for r in rows]
outs = llm.chat(msgs, SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=64),
                chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False})
answers = [letter(o.outputs[0].text) for o in outs]
print("accuracy", sum(a == r["answer"] for a, r in zip(answers, rows)) / len(rows))
json.dump(answers, open(out, "w"))  # compare two runs answer by answer
```

```python
# ttft.py MODEL [BACKEND]: one-image requests, max_tokens=1, new image each time.
import base64, io, os, statistics, sys, time
os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0"
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

kw = dict(model=sys.argv[1], max_model_len=4096, max_num_seqs=1,
          limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1, "video": 0},
          gpu_memory_utilization=0.85, seed=0)
if len(sys.argv) > 2:
    kw["mm_encoder_attn_backend"] = sys.argv[2]
llm = LLM(**kw)
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
for w, h in [(336, 336), (1024, 800)]:
    times = []
    for i in range(3 + 15):
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        Image.fromarray(rng.integers(0, 255, (h, w, 3), dtype=np.uint8)).save(buf, "PNG")
        url = "data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode()
        msg = [{"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": url}},
            {"type": "text", "text": "Describe the image."}]}]
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        llm.chat(msg, SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1), use_tqdm=False)
        if i >= 3:
            times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1e3)
    print(f"{w}x{h}: median {statistics.median(times):.1f} ms, "
          f"stdev {statistics.pstdev(times):.1f} ms")
```

</details>

## Details

Three commits:

1. **[NFC]** Move the `cu_seqlens` graph-buffer padding shared by Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL to `MMEncoderAttention.cu_seqlens_buffer_padding(backend)`.
2. **Encoder CUDA graphs** (+18 lines): `EncoderItemSpec.eager_only` and the clear `TORCH_SDPA` error.
3. **Gemma 4:** new `gemma4_vision.py` (440 lines) while `gemma4_mm.py` drops 679, net −12 non-test lines. Removes the resolution buckets, `_encoder_chunk`, the tower LoRA padding and the row-width graph axis. Graphs size their sequence slots (`budget // 35`) and `max_seqlen` (configured `max_soft_tokens`) to what they can hold; larger items run eager.

- **Behavior change:** Gemma 4 with `TORCH_SDPA` (RDNA default) and `cudagraph_mm_encoder` (off by default) now needs another backend, e.g. `TRITON_ATTN`; documented in `docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md`.
- **Same as the old tower:** replicated linears (DP is #60314), and separate q/k/v and gate/up projections, because each clipped linear has its own bounds.
- **Numerics:** `GELUTanh` is used directly because `get_act_fn` swaps in exact GELU on ROCm. vLLM's `RMSNorm` rounds differently from transformers', which MMStar covers.
- **FlashInfer:** a new `separate_qkv` flag on `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`; GQA is rejected.

Hello there @Isotr0py. I think you reviewed several PRs regarding bringing Gemma4 to the current standard path for MMEncoderAttention, but many of them missed something. I tried to bring all your requests into a single place. Could you provide me pointers on what extra things I could be missing on this PR?

Thanks for upstreaming this, @roberteg16. I validated it on NVIDIA H100 (SM90), rebased locally onto `2d858ac60a`. Two things break there; both fixes are below.

**1. The Triton case of `test_gemma4_vision.py` fails on NVIDIA**

```
FAILED test_packed_tower_matches_transformers[False-AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN]
FAILED test_packed_tower_matches_transformers[True-AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN]
Greatest absolute difference: 0.0222 (up to 0.001 allowed)
```

On NVIDIA GPUs, Triton runs fp32 `tl.dot` in TF32. With `TRITON_F32_DEFAULT=ieee` the test passes at 1e-3. Fix: keep 1e-3 for SDPA and allow 3e-2 for Triton on CUDA (https://github.com/hnt2601/vllm/commit/802ac1fcd3e11d824edbb84542f425880a3ec202).

**2. Packing the whole encoder batch into one eager call costs KV cache**

`google/gemma-4-31B-it`, FA, eager, `max_model_len=8192`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9`, same H100:

| | peak activation (profile) | available KV | starts? |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 2.78 GiB | 8.31 GiB | yes |
| this PR | **3.83 GiB** | 6.09 GiB | **no**: needs 6.89 GiB for one 8192-token request |
| this PR + cap below | 2.81 GiB | 7.99 GiB | yes |

The memory profile now runs the tower on every dummy image in a single call, so the encoder's peak activations grow. Fix: cap each eager call at 4 × 1120 soft tokens (https://github.com/hnt2601/vllm/commit/f77e4f64948608c2c7bb17f2930b8bec0603eeed). Tower LoRA still uses one call, because the adapter mapping spans the encoder batch.

**H100 results with both fixes** (`google/gemma-4-31B-it`, BF16, 1× H100 80GB):

| ViT backend | eager | `cudagraph_mm_encoder` |
|---|---|---|
| FLASH_ATTN (auto on SM90, head_dim 72) | OK | OK (KV +6.7% vs main's graphs) |
| FLASHINFER | OK | OK |
| TRITON_ATTN | OK | OK |
| TORCH_SDPA | OK | startup error (intended) |

Results are greedy over 6 image prompts with 64 tokens, compared against main. Every divergence falls within the top-5 logprobs, and FA vs SDPA on the native tower diverge by the same amount, so it is bf16 noise. Graph runs used MRV1, because encoder graphs on MRV2 OOM during capture for 31B on main as well. That MRV2 issue is unrelated to this PR, and I'll file it separately.

These fixes are in #65591. It is stacked on this PR and only adds the commits above. I'll keep it a draft until this PR lands; feel free to pull the commits in here instead if you prefer.

+class Gemma4VisionClippableLinear(nn.Module):
+    """Linear layer whose input and output are clamped to checkpoint bounds."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: Gemma4VisionConfig,
+        input_size: int,
+        output_size: int,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.use_clipped_linears = config.use_clipped_linears
+        self.linear = ReplicatedLinear(
+            input_size,
+            output_size,
+            bias=False,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "linear"),
+            return_bias=False,
+        )
+        if self.use_clipped_linears:
+            self.input_min: torch.Tensor
+            self.input_max: torch.Tensor
+            self.output_min: torch.Tensor
+            self.output_max: torch.Tensor
+            self.register_buffer("input_min", torch.tensor(-float("inf")))
+            self.register_buffer("input_max", torch.tensor(float("inf")))
+            self.register_buffer("output_min", torch.tensor(-float("inf")))
+            self.register_buffer("output_max", torch.tensor(float("inf")))
+
+    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if self.use_clipped_linears:
+            x = torch.clamp(x, self.input_min, self.input_max)
+        x = self.linear(x)
+        if self.use_clipped_linears:
+            x = torch.clamp(x, self.output_min, self.output_max)
+        return x
+

+class Gemma4VisionPatchEmbedder(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: Gemma4VisionConfig,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.input_proj = ReplicatedLinear(
+            3 * config.patch_size**2,
+            config.hidden_size,
+            bias=False,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "input_proj"),
+            return_bias=False,
+        )
+        self.position_embedding_table = nn.Parameter(
+            torch.empty(2, config.position_embedding_size, config.hidden_size)
+        )
+
+    def forward(
+        self, pixel_values: torch.Tensor, positions: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        table = self.position_embedding_table
+        pixel_values = (2 * (pixel_values - 0.5)).to(table.dtype)
+        position_embeddings = table[0][positions[:, 0]] + table[1][positions[:, 1]]
+        return self.input_proj(pixel_values) + position_embeddings
+

+class Gemma4VisionAttention(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: Gemma4VisionConfig,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.num_heads = config.num_attention_heads
+        self.num_kv_heads = config.num_key_value_heads
+        self.head_dim = config.head_dim
+        hidden_size = config.hidden_size
+
+        linear = partial(Gemma4VisionClippableLinear, config, quant_config=quant_config)
+        q_size = self.num_heads * self.head_dim
+        kv_size = self.num_kv_heads * self.head_dim
+        self.q_proj = linear(hidden_size, q_size, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "q_proj"))
+        self.k_proj = linear(
+            hidden_size, kv_size, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "k_proj")
+        )
+        self.v_proj = linear(
+            hidden_size, kv_size, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "v_proj")
+        )
+        self.o_proj = linear(q_size, hidden_size, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "o_proj"))
+        self.q_norm = RMSNorm(self.head_dim, eps=config.rms_norm_eps)
+        self.k_norm = RMSNorm(self.head_dim, eps=config.rms_norm_eps)
+        self.v_norm = RMSNorm(self.head_dim, eps=config.rms_norm_eps, has_weight=False)
+        self.apply_rotary_emb = ApplyRotaryEmb(enforce_enable=True)
+        self.attn = MMEncoderAttention(
+            self.num_heads,
+            self.head_dim,
+            scale=1.0,
+            num_kv_heads=self.num_kv_heads,
+            prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "attn"),
+        )
+
+    def _rope(
+        self, x: torch.Tensor, cos: torch.Tensor, sin: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        half = self.head_dim // 2
+        return torch.cat(
+            (
+                self.apply_rotary_emb(x[..., :half], cos[0], sin[0]),
+                self.apply_rotary_emb(x[..., half:], cos[1], sin[1]),
+            ),
+            dim=-1,
+        )
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        cos: torch.Tensor,
+        sin: torch.Tensor,
+        cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
+        max_seqlen: torch.Tensor,
+        sequence_lengths: torch.Tensor | None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        num_tokens = x.shape[0]
+        q = self.q_norm(self.q_proj(x).view(-1, self.head_dim))
+        k = self.k_norm(self.k_proj(x).view(-1, self.head_dim))
+        v = self.v_norm(self.v_proj(x).view(-1, self.head_dim))
+        q = self._rope(q.view(num_tokens, self.num_heads, self.head_dim), cos, sin)
+        k = self._rope(k.view(num_tokens, self.num_kv_heads, self.head_dim), cos, sin)
+        v = v.view(num_tokens, self.num_kv_heads, self.head_dim)
+        out = self.attn(
+            q.unsqueeze(0),
+            k.unsqueeze(0),
+            v.unsqueeze(0),
+            cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
+            max_seqlen=max_seqlen,
+            sequence_lengths=sequence_lengths,
+        )
+        return self.o_proj(out.reshape(num_tokens, -1))
+
+
+class Gemma4VisionMLP(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: Gemma4VisionConfig,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        linear = partial(Gemma4VisionClippableLinear, config, quant_config=quant_config)
+        hidden_size, intermediate_size = config.hidden_size, config.intermediate_size
+        self.gate_proj = linear(
+            hidden_size, intermediate_size, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "gate_proj")
+        )
+        self.up_proj = linear(
+            hidden_size, intermediate_size, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "up_proj")
+        )
+        self.down_proj = linear(
+            intermediate_size, hidden_size, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "down_proj")
+        )
+        # get_act_fn swaps gelu_pytorch_tanh for the exact GELU on ROCm, for
+        # torch.compile; this tower is not compiled, so keep the model's tanh.
+        self.act_fn = (
+            GELUTanh()
+            if config.hidden_activation == "gelu_pytorch_tanh"
+            else get_act_fn(config.hidden_activation)
+        )
+
+    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.down_proj(self.act_fn(self.gate_proj(x)) * self.up_proj(x))
+
+
+class Gemma4VisionEncoderLayer(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: Gemma4VisionConfig,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.self_attn = Gemma4VisionAttention(
+            config, quant_config=quant_config, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "self_attn")
+        )
+        self.mlp = Gemma4VisionMLP(
+            config, quant_config=quant_config, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "mlp")
+        )
+        hidden_size, eps = config.hidden_size, config.rms_norm_eps
+        self.input_layernorm = RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=eps)
+        self.post_attention_layernorm = RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=eps)
+        self.pre_feedforward_layernorm = RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=eps)
+        self.post_feedforward_layernorm = RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=eps)
+
+    def forward(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor, **attn_kwargs) -> torch.Tensor:
+        x = self.self_attn(self.input_layernorm(hidden_states), **attn_kwargs)
+        hidden_states = hidden_states + self.post_attention_layernorm(x)
+        x = self.mlp(self.pre_feedforward_layernorm(hidden_states))
+        return hidden_states + self.post_feedforward_layernorm(x)
+
+
+class Gemma4VisionEncoder(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: Gemma4VisionConfig,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        assert config.rope_parameters is not None
+        # Axial 2D RoPE: the first half of each head rotates by the patch's
+        # x, the second half by its y, each with head_dim / 2 rotary dims.
+        self.rotary_emb = get_rope(
+            head_size=config.head_dim,
+            max_position=config.position_embedding_size,
+            is_neox_style=True,
+            rope_parameters={
+                "rope_theta": config.rope_parameters["rope_theta"],
+                "partial_rotary_factor": 0.5,
+            },
+        )
+        self.layers = nn.ModuleList(
+            [
+                Gemma4VisionEncoderLayer(
+                    config,
+                    quant_config=quant_config,
+                    prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, f"layers.{i}"),
+                )
+                for i in range(config.num_hidden_layers)
+            ]
+        )
+
+
+class Gemma4VisionModel(nn.Module):
+    """Encodes packed patches and pools each image's ``k x k`` blocks into
+    soft tokens."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: Gemma4VisionConfig,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.config = config
+        self.patch_embedder = Gemma4VisionPatchEmbedder(
+            config,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "patch_embedder"),
+        )
+        self.encoder = Gemma4VisionEncoder(
+            config, quant_config=quant_config, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "encoder")
+        )
+        if config.standardize:

+            self.std_scale: torch.Tensor

+
+        self.attn_backend = get_vit_attn_backend(
+            head_size=config.head_dim, dtype=torch.get_default_dtype()
+        )
+        # FlashInfer reads q, k and v with one per-token stride: no GQA.
+        if (
+            self.attn_backend == AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHINFER
+            and config.num_key_value_heads != config.num_attention_heads
+        ):
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "FLASHINFER for Gemma 4's vision tower needs as many key/value "
+                "heads as query heads."
+            )
+        self.fp8_padded_hidden_size = get_fp8_padded_hidden_size(
+            config.num_attention_heads, config.head_dim
+        )
+
+    @property
+    def dtype(self) -> torch.dtype:
+        return self.patch_embedder.position_embedding_table.dtype
+
+    @property
+    def device(self) -> torch.device:
+        return self.patch_embedder.position_embedding_table.device
+
+    def prepare_encoder_metadata(
+        self,
+        positions: Sequence[np.ndarray],
+        *,
+        max_num_seqs: int | None = None,
+        max_seqlen_override: int | None = None,
+        device: torch.device | None = None,
+    ) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+        """Host-side metadata for packed images, shared by the eager path and
+        CUDA graph capture and replay.
+
+        Args:
+            positions: ``(x, y)`` patch positions of each image or video
+                frame, padding excluded.
+            max_num_seqs: Pad ``cu_seqlens`` with empty sequences to this
+                many sequences (CUDA graph buffers).
+            max_seqlen_override: ``max_seqlen`` to use instead of the longest
+                sequence (CUDA graph capture, where it is baked in).
+            device: Device for the tensors. Defaults to the tower's.
+
+        """
+        if device is None:
+            device = self.device
+        k = self.config.pooling_kernel_size
+
+        seqlens = np.array([len(p) for p in positions], dtype=np.int32)
+        cu_seqlens = np.concatenate([[0], seqlens.cumsum()]).astype(np.int32)
+        # The processor lays out each image's patches in row-major order, in a
+        # grid whose sides are multiples of the pooling kernel.
+        grids = []
+        for pos in positions:
+            columns = int(pos[:, 0].max()) + 1
+            rows = len(pos) // columns
+            patches = np.arange(len(pos))
+            if (
+                rows % k
+                or columns % k
+                or not np.array_equal(pos[:, 0], patches % columns)
+                or not np.array_equal(pos[:, 1], patches // columns)
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Expected a row-major grid of patches with sides that are "
+                    f"multiples of {k}, got {len(pos)} patches in "
+                    f"{columns} columns."
+                )
+            grids.append((rows, columns))
+        pool_gather_idx = _build_merge_gather_idx(grids, (k, k))
+        if max_num_seqs is not None and len(seqlens) < max_num_seqs:
+            cu_seqlens = np.pad(
+                cu_seqlens, (0, max_num_seqs - len(seqlens)), mode="edge"
+            )
+
+        if max_seqlen_override is not None:
+            max_seqlen = max_seqlen_override
+        else:
+            max_seqlen = MMEncoderAttention.compute_max_seqlen(
+                self.attn_backend, cu_seqlens
+            )
+        metadata = {
+            "pixel_position_ids": async_tensor_h2d(
+                np.concatenate(positions).astype(np.int64), device=device
+            ),
+            "pool_gather_idx": async_tensor_h2d(pool_gather_idx, device=device),
+            "cu_seqlens": MMEncoderAttention.maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens(
+                self.attn_backend,
+                cu_seqlens,
+                self.config.num_attention_heads * self.config.head_dim,
+                1,
+                device,
+                fp8_padded_hidden_size=self.fp8_padded_hidden_size,
+                separate_qkv=True,
+            ),
+            # On the host: backends read it there, and CUDA graphs bake it in.
+            "max_seqlen": torch.tensor(max_seqlen, dtype=torch.int32),
+        }
+        sequence_lengths = MMEncoderAttention.maybe_compute_seq_lens(
+            self.attn_backend, cu_seqlens, device
+        )
+        if sequence_lengths is not None:  # FlashInfer
+            metadata["sequence_lengths"] = sequence_lengths
+        return metadata
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        pixel_values: torch.Tensor,
+        encoder_metadata: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor],
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Encode packed patches ``(num_patches, 3 * patch_size**2)`` into
+        soft tokens ``(num_patches / k**2, hidden_size)``."""
+        positions = encoder_metadata["pixel_position_ids"]
+        hidden_states = self.patch_embedder(pixel_values, positions)
+        cos, sin = self.encoder.rotary_emb.get_cos_sin(
+            self.config.position_embedding_size
+        )
+        # (2, num_patches, head_dim / 4): x's tables, then y's, each contiguous.
+        cos, sin = cos[positions.T], sin[positions.T]
+        for layer in self.encoder.layers:
+            hidden_states = layer(
+                hidden_states,
+                cos=cos,
+                sin=sin,
+                cu_seqlens=encoder_metadata["cu_seqlens"],
+                max_seqlen=encoder_metadata["max_seqlen"],
+                sequence_lengths=encoder_metadata.get("sequence_lengths"),
+            )
+        return self._pool(hidden_states, encoder_metadata["pool_gather_idx"])
+
+    def _pool(
+        self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor, pool_gather_idx: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        hidden_size = hidden_states.shape[-1]
+        k = self.config.pooling_kernel_size
+        blocks = patch_merger_packed(hidden_states, pool_gather_idx, (k, k))
+        # Average and scale in float32 like transformers: the sqrt(hidden_size)
+        # scaling can exceed the float16 range before standardization.
+        pooled = blocks.float().mean(1).to(hidden_states.dtype).float()
+        pooled = pooled * hidden_size**0.5
+        if self.config.standardize:
+            pooled = (pooled - self.std_bias.float()) * self.std_scale.float()
+        return pooled.to(hidden_states.dtype)

```
FAILED test_packed_tower_matches_transformers[True-AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN]
Greatest absolute difference: 0.0222 (up to 0.001 allowed)
```

On NVIDIA GPUs, Triton runs fp32 `tl.dot` in TF32. With `TRITON_F32_DEFAULT=ieee` the test passes at 1e-3. Fix: keep 1e-3 for SDPA and allow 3e-2 for Triton on CUDA (https://github.com/hnt2601/vllm/commit/802ac1fcd3e11d824edbb84542f425880a3ec202).

**2. Packing the whole encoder batch into one eager call costs KV cache**

`google/gemma-4-31B-it`, FA, eager, `max_model_len=8192`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9`, same H100:

| | peak activation (profile) | available KV | starts? |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 2.78 GiB | 8.31 GiB | yes |
| this PR | **3.83 GiB** | 6.09 GiB | **no**: needs 6.89 GiB for one 8192-token request |
| this PR + cap below | 2.81 GiB | 7.99 GiB | yes |

The memory profile now runs the tower on every dummy image in a single call, so the encoder's peak activations grow. Fix: cap each eager call at 4 × 1120 soft tokens (https://github.com/hnt2601/vllm/commit/f77e4f64948608c2c7bb17f2930b8bec0603eeed). Tower LoRA still uses one call, because the adapter mapping spans the encoder batch.

**H100 results with both fixes** (`google/gemma-4-31B-it`, BF16, 1× H100 80GB):

| ViT backend | eager | `cudagraph_mm_encoder` |
|---|---|---|
| FLASH_ATTN (auto on SM90, head_dim 72) | OK | OK (KV +6.7% vs main's graphs) |
| FLASHINFER | OK | OK |
| TRITON_ATTN | OK | OK |
| TORCH_SDPA | OK | startup error (intended) |

Results are greedy over 6 image prompts with 64 tokens, compared against main. Every divergence falls within the top-5 logprobs, and FA vs SDPA on the native tower diverge by the same amount, so it is bf16 noise. Graph runs used MRV1, because encoder graphs on MRV2 OOM during capture for 31B on main as well. That MRV2 issue is unrelated to this PR, and I'll file it separately.

These fixes are in #65591. It is stacked on this PR and only adds the commits above. I'll keep it a draft until this PR lands; feel free to pull the commits in here instead if you prefer.

The H100 testing and this comment were AI-assisted (Claude Code); I checked the results.
